Corfu Old Romaniote Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kerkira, Greece

Demolished. This is the Romaniot counterpart to Corfu's Old Sephardic Jewish Cemetery, presumed founded in the Middle Ages — earlier than the Sephardi cemetery, reflecting the Romaniot community's older presence on the island before Sephardi, Italian, and Sicilian immigrants arrived from the late 14th century onward. Both Corfu cemeteries met the same fate: entirely destroyed, with a school, fire station, parking lot, and residential buildings now covering the shared site. The community itself endured German bombing in 1943 and the 1944 deportation of some 1,800 Jews to Auschwitz, surviving afterward only as a small, partly rebuilt population.
